children: Our Bureau New Delhi: Oil and Natural Gas Corp (ONGC) has struck gas at a deepwater well in the Mahanadi offshore basin off the Odisha coast, the state-run explorer said in a statement on Monday. ONGC struck gas on September 18 at the MN-DW18-1-H-D well, about 43 km off Konark, at a depth of 1,441-1,452 metres.

The well was drilled to a total depth of 1,623 metres under the country's Samudra Manthan deepwater exploration programme. The well, the first drilled by ONGC in the Mahanadi basin under the current campaign, has been flowing gas with "encouraging flow and reservoir pressure" for the past three days, the company said.

The discovery is subject to further appraisal and commercial evaluation. ONGC said the find, along with other discoveries in the area, could potentially be developed through shared facilities enabled by the Petroleum and Natural Gas Rules, 2025, allowing deepwater resources to be brought into production. The well was spudded on July 25 by petroleum minister Hardeep Singh Puri.

title: ONGC Finds Gas Off Odisha Coast
